topic: Lambda Type: Unique Closure Class Generation
explanation: Every lambda expression in the source code causes the compiler to generate a unique, unnamed type known as the *closure class*. All runtime closure objects corresponding to that single lambda expression are instances of this unique class. Why It Matters: Because each lambda expression produces a distinct type, it is impossible to name the type directly. This necessitates the use of `auto` when defining a variable to hold a closure object, or relying on type erasure mechanisms like `std::function` (which may incur overhead).
practical_example: A developer attempts to pass a lambda closure to a function that expects a specific type signature, but without using `auto` or templates. They must use `std::function` to erase the unique closure type, potentially trading performance for flexibility.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
